title: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report (September 2026)
source: EST: investing.com's OPEC Monthly Report calendar page lists the next release as "Sep 10, 2026 10:00" (London), against a printed history of Aug 12, Jun 11, May 13, Apr 13, Mar 11 2026 and Dec 11, Nov 12, Oct 13, Sep 11 2025 that matches OPEC's standing mid-month cadence. AGGREGATOR-SOURCED AND LABELLED AS SUCH — opec.org was not fetched for this date, so it has not been checked against a primary. Same aggregator whose IEA Oil Market Report table was independently verified 4/4 against IEA's own blob-hosted PDF filenames during the iea-omr-2026-09-11 initial research, which is a reliability check on the table and not on this row. Discovered during the iea-omr-2026-09-11 initial research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The producer cartel's own number, and the middle leg of an agency triple this calendar tracked only one third of: EIA STEO 2026-09-09, OPEC MOMR 2026-09-10, IEA OMR 2026-09-11 — three forecasting agencies publishing on three consecutive sessions. Its research value is the question the iea-omr-2026-09-11 research left open: the two consumer-side agencies disagree by 51% on the same month's Gulf shut-in (EIA ~5.5 mb/d vs IEA 8.3 mb/d for July 2026), so no single supply figure is currently a fact and the producer side's read is the one independent number nobody has looked at. Filed low on the same reasoning as eia-steo-2026-09-09 and iea-omr-2026-09-11: a forecast publication sets no policy and moves no equity tape, and the OMR base rate measured on 2026-09-06 (0 of 13 releases beating the ordinary same-hour p95 on either crude benchmark) is the closest available prior for what a monthly oil report does to the tape. It also lands on an already-thick session — PPI, the ECB decision, the 30Y bond auction, the 10y20y buyback operation and a coupon announcement all print 2026-09-10 — so treat it as a data source to read after the fact, never as a scheduled catalyst.
